icd.name: FMOFP MIL-STD-1553B Bus ICD
icd.revision: First draft, derived from FMOFP/rtAddressConfig.xml and FMOFP/MIL_STD_1553B/message_schemas.py.
Alee's answers 1-3: display addresses accepted; BIT merged into avionics (RT 1), FM fitness and SW configuration folded in as well; bus controller confirmed as its own process. RT 24-26 freed.

Alee's answers 4-10: UDP transport accepted; legacy WEATHER mode dropped as unnecessary; every TBD value defined from the code that uses it; heading and yaw are true. Command parameters nothing consumed were removed.

First partition (flight control): the plant terminal RT 27 and PLANT_SENSORS, relayed to the FCS as FCS_SENSORS; FCS_GCAS_ALERTS and FCS_PERF_STATUS outputs; the relays section, which also makes the BC deliver the MFD's radar commands. Kevin owns the ICD from this revision.

Navigation and flight management partitions: PLANT_GPS pseudoranges, the nav terminal's NAV_SENSORS/NAV_GPS inputs and NAV_SOLUTION; the FMS's relayed inputs (FMS_ATTITUDE_IN, FMS_SENSORS, FMS_NAV_SOLUTION), FMS_FLIGHT_DATA (replacing the FMS_DATA block), FMS_FLIGHT_MODE_CMD, FMS_CONTROL_CMD/STATUS, FMS_ENERGY; FMS_STATUS, FMS_ATTITUDE_STATUS and FMS_NAV_UPDATE_STATUS grown to report what the Python returned. Double-word (32-bit) fields; a producer may be relayed to several consumers. Enums fms_flight_mode, countermeasures_state, targeting_state, weapons_state.

Weather radar partition: PLANT_WEATHER (the simulated storm cells and stratiform area, moved by the plant) relayed to the radar as RDR_WX_WEATHER; RDR_WX_SCAN; the RDR_WX_PRODUCTS block (VIL and precipitation points, storm cells, precipitation areas, wind shear events, turbulence cells of one scan), replacing the RDR_WX_VIL and RDR_WX_PRECIP streams. Block payload layouts: a header and record sections, generated for both sides. Enums precip_type, shear_severity, turbulence_category.

Terrain-following radar partition: the plant gains the terrain (PLANT_TERRAIN, the elevation profile ahead of the aircraft, a block relayed to the radar as RDR_TFR_TERRAIN - the first block relay and the first receive block); the radar gets the aircraft state as RDR_TFR_SENSORS and publishes RDR_TFR_GUIDANCE and the RDR_TFR_ELEVATION block (the assessed profile and the path commands). The flight control computer takes its terrain clearance from the radar (FCS_TERRAIN) instead of the plant: PLANT_SENSORS loses terrain_clearance. Enums clearance_level, terrain_warning, path_reason.

The first displays on the bus. The radar display (RT 15) receives the weather and terrain-following radars' status, scan summary and guidance by relay and their products as receive blocks (DSP_RDR_WX_PRODUCTS, DSP_RDR_TFR_ELEVATION), and is the radars' control panel: the radar commands move from the MFD (MFD_RDR_*_CMD, never implemented) to DSP_RDR_*_CMD. The PFD (RT 11) receives FMS_FLIGHT_DATA, FMS_STATUS and FMS_ATTITUDE_STATUS by relay (PFD_FLIGHT_DATA, PFD_FMS_STATUS, PFD_ATTITUDE_STATUS). A command whose cmd_seq is 0 is no command: an unloaded command subaddress reads as zeros.

enum.doc: FMS flight mode (fmsControl.available_modes), numbered as flightManagementSystem.send_fms_data did. Each selects a flight profile - max bank 30/80/45/60/90 deg, max pitch 20/60/30/45/85 deg, max g 2.5/9/5/7/9.5, max AoA 15/25/20/22/30 deg, engine power 0.7/1.0/0.6/0.9/1.0, turn rate limit 3/20/5/15/25 deg/s - for NORMAL/COMBAT/STEALTH/TRAINING/EMERGENCY
fmsControl tactical_systems countermeasures, set by the flight mode
fmsControl tactical_systems targeting, set by the flight mode
fmsControl tactical_systems weapons, set by the flight mode

Precipitation type in a weather radar product. The point product (precipitation_data_generator_sync) classifies by rate: HAIL above 50 mm/h, MIXED above 25, RAIN above 10, else RAIN or SNOW; the area product (precipitation_analysis) by reflectivity: HAIL above 55 dBZ, HEAVY_RAIN above 45, else RAIN
Wind shear event severity (weather_processor.WindShearProcessor): LOW from 15 kt/nm, MODERATE above 20, SEVERE above 30
Turbulence category by eddy dissipation rate proxy (weather_processor.TurbulenceProcessor, the FAA AC 120-88A bands): LIGHT from 0.1, MODERATE from 0.2, SEVERE from 0.4, EXTREME from 0.6
Terrain clearance advisory level (tfr_processor.ClearanceManager): CLEAR at 600 m of clearance or more, LOW from 300 m, CAUTION from 150 m, PULL_UP below that. NONE when no assessment exists
Terrain feature warning at a profile sample (tfr_radar._check_terrain_warnings): HIGH_TERRAIN above 1500 m, else STEEP_TERRAIN more than 300 m from the 1000 m reference

Why a terrain-following altitude command exists (tfr_processor.PathOptimiser): TERRAIN_AVOIDANCE for the rate-limited commands along the look-ahead window, CLEARANCE for the final command that clears the highest terrain in the window. OBSTACLE is reserved

message.title: Weather radar scan summary
message.doc: What the last completed scan found, for the display's header and for anyone who does not reassemble the RDR_WX_PRODUCTS block. While NORMAL in an operating mode the radar sweeps the full circle over 60 minor frames (1.2 s), six azimuth degrees per frame, rendering the volume from the weather truth it latched when the sweep began; the products of a scan are published as one block when the scan completes, and products_version is the block version carrying them. The counts are what was detected before the block's record limits were applied.

field.name: scan_id
field.doc: Id of the last completed scan, increments mod 256

field.name: mode
field.doc: Mode the scan was made in; NONE when no scan has completed since the mode was left

field.name: microburst
field.doc: 1 = a wind shear event with microburst divergence was found (WINDSHEAR mode)

field.name: elevations
field.doc: Elevation angles in the scan's volume coverage pattern: 4 for SURVEILLANCE, 7 for MAPPING and PRECIPITATION, 1 for TURBULENCE and WINDSHEAR

field.name: products_version
field.doc: RDR_WX_PRODUCTS block version carrying this scan's products

field.name: range_km
field.doc: Instrumented range in effect; range bins beyond it are not scanned

field.name: tilt
field.doc: Antenna tilt in effect, reported as commanded; the sensor model has no antenna to tilt

field.name: storm_cells

field.name: precip_areas

field.name: scan_frame

field.name: set_clearance

message.title: Terrain-following guidance
message.doc: What the terrain-following radar makes of the terrain ahead, from tfr_processor.py: the clearance assessment of the latest profile against the aircraft's altitude (ClearanceManager.assess_profile: the minimum clearance, the advisory level, which latches at the worst level seen until a profile with no advisory at all), the first altitude command of the path optimiser (PathOptimiser.compute_path, flown at the set clearance), and whether any sample carries a terrain warning (tfr_radar._check_terrain_warnings). Every operating mode produces it, as the Python's radar ran both processors whatever its mode. The flight control computer receives it as FCS_TERRAIN; its minimum clearance is what the ground collision avoidance TERRAIN alert tests. Clearances are negative when the terrain is above the aircraft.

field.name: clearance_ssm
field.doc: NORMAL while the radar is operating with a terrain profile and the aircraft's altitude; NO_COMPUTED_DATA otherwise, when every value below is 0

field.name: mode
field.doc: Mode the guidance was computed in; NONE when not operating

field.name: steep_terrain
field.doc: 1 = a sample is more than 300 m from the 1000 m reference (and not high terrain)

field.name: commands_valid
field.doc: 1 = the path optimiser produced at least one command

field.name: terrain_clearance
field.doc: Altitude minus the terrain at the first sample, under the aircraft

field.name: min_clearance
field.doc: The smallest clearance over the whole profile

field.name: commanded_altitude
field.doc: The first path command's altitude (MSL); 0 when commands_valid is 0

field.name: set_clearance

message.title: Sensed flight state, for navigation
message.doc: PLANT_SENSORS relayed to navigation. Airspeed (as ground speed), heading and vertical speed drive the dead-reckoning prediction between GPS fixes, with the rates flightManagementSystem.update_flight_data derived.

message.title: GPS pseudoranges, for navigation
message.doc: PLANT_GPS relayed to navigation, which solves the position fix from it (globalPositionSystem.GPSReceiver._wls_solve, then _ecef_to_wgs84).

message.title: Navigation solution
message.doc: The fused position (fuseData.NavDataFusion: one scalar Kalman filter per axis, predicted by dead reckoning every frame and corrected by each GPS fix). position_ssm and altitude_ssm are NO_COMPUTED_DATA until the first fix has been incorporated; after that the estimate is always computed, and gps_valid plus fix_age say how fresh the last fix is. gps_valid is 1 when the last GPS epoch gave a fix (at least 4 satellites, solvable geometry). clock_bias is the receiver clock bias the solver estimated.

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Height above the WGS-84 ellipsoid, as the GPS reports it

field.name: fix_count
field.doc: Fixes incorporated since start, saturates at 255

field.name: fix_age
field.doc: Seconds since the last fix, saturates at 255; 255 before the first

field.name: clock_bias
field.doc: Receiver clock bias from the solver

message.doc: fmsControl.set_mode: NORMAL, COMBAT, STEALTH, TRAINING or EMERGENCY. Selects the flight profile limits that attitude commands and maneuvers are held to, and the tactical systems states in FMS_STATUS.

message.title: Attitude command status
message.doc: The attitude the FMS holds after envelope limiting (fmsControl.update_attitude): the commanded values, absent ones taken from the measured attitude, each held to the flight profile of the mode in force. A *_limited bit is 1 while that limit is active (the Python's envelope_warnings). The SSMs are NO_COMPUTED_DATA until the first attitude command. The measured attitude is in FMS_FLIGHT_DATA.

field.name: bank_limited
field.doc: Roll held to the profile's max_bank_angle (BANK_ANGLE)

field.name: roll_rate_limited

field.name: pitch_rate_limited

message.title: Autopilot target status
message.doc: The targets in force after fmsControl.set_autopilot_targets limited them: altitude 0-60000 ft, airspeed 100-1000 kt, heading wrapped to 0-360, vertical speed -8000 .. 6000 ft/min. Before any command they are the Python's initial targets: 30000 ft, 450 kt, 0 deg, 0 ft/min.

field.name: dive_angle
field.doc: DIVE only; 0 means the FMS default of -30 deg

message.title: FMS flight data
message.doc: What flightManagementSystem.get_flight_data() gave the displays: attitude from the FCS (FMS_ATTITUDE_IN), air data from the sensors (FMS_SENSORS), position and fused altitude from navigation (FMS_NAV_SOLUTION), and the values the Python derived - mach = airspeed / (661.4788 x 0.98); energy_state = min(100, (0.5 x 15000 x v^2 + 15000 x 9.81 x h) / 1e10 x 100) with v in m/s from airspeed and h in m from nav_altitude. ground_speed is the airspeed, since the plant has no wind. track and sideslip were never computed by the Python and are sent NO_COMPUTED_DATA. Replaces the FMS_DATA block of v1.

field.name: nav_altitude

message.title: Thrust and landing gear status
message.doc: fmsControl.set_thrust holds thrust to 0.1 .. 0.9 (1.0 with the afterburner lit), sets throttle_position = int(thrust x 100), lights the afterburner above 0.9 and puts it out below 0.85. Before any command: thrust 0.5, throttle 50, afterburner off, gear UP.

message.title: Energy maneuverability
message.doc: fmsControl.calculate_energy_maneuverability(), from nav_altitude, airspeed, angle of attack and the flight profile's engine_power and max_g_force: specific excess power Ps = v (T - D) / W with T = engine_power x 150000 N, D = 0.5 x 1.225 e^(-h/10000) v^2 (0.02 + |aoa|/100) x 30, W = 15000 x 9.81; sustained turn rate = deg(g sqrt((T/W)^2 - 1) / v) when T/W is above 1, else 0; instantaneous turn rate = deg(g sqrt(max_g^2 - 1) / v); climb = Ps x 196.85 ft/min; energy_advantage = 10 Ps. v is at least 1 m/s in the turn rates.

message.doc: Relayed into RT 9 SA 3, when that radar is ported.

message.title: Radar display command to the targeting radar
message.doc: Relayed into RT 9 SA 4, when that radar is ported.

message.title: Radar display command to the AEWC radar
message.doc: Relayed into RT 9 SA 5, when that radar is ported.

message.title: FMS flight data as received by the PFD
message.doc: What pfd.update_flight_data() read from get_flight_data(): attitude, velocity, navigation, tactical and status. A field whose SSM is not NORMAL is left out of the dictionary the display reads, so its tape draws the amber X (README section 4).

message.title: FMS status as received by the PFD
message.doc: The flight mode's profile limits (maximum g and angle of attack) that the PFD's tactical indicators scale against.

message.title: Attitude command status as received by the PFD
message.doc: The limited bits are the envelope warnings the PFD lists (BANK ANGLE, PITCH ANGLE, ROLL RATE, PITCH RATE, YAW RATE), as fmsControl.get_tactical_status() gave them.

message.title: Sensed flight state from the plant
message.doc: What the aircraft's sensors would measure, published by the simulated aircraft. Ranges follow flightControlComputer.py (altitude 0-60000 ft, speed 100-1000 kt, pitch +-45, roll +-60, AoA 0-25, g 0.5-9) with headroom. Each quantity carries its own SSM so a sensor can fail alone.

field.name: spare_1a
field.doc: Was the terrain clearance SSM until v1.4

field.name: g_force
field.doc: Normal load factor, 1.0 in level flight

message.title: GPS pseudoranges from the plant
message.doc: What the simulated GPS receiver measures each epoch: for every satellite of the 12-satellite constellation of globalPositionSystem._build_constellation() that is at least 5 degrees above the horizon, pseudorange = geometric range + c x (receiver clock bias - satellite clock bias) + measurement noise (3 m, 1 sigma). The noise is drawn once per epoch here, in the plant; the solver in the navigation terminal is deterministic. epoch increments with each new set; a pseudorange whose satellite bit is 0 in visible_mask is not valid.

field.name: epoch
field.doc: Increments (mod 16) with every new measurement set

field.name: visible_mask
field.doc: Bit n-1 = satellite n (1-12) has a valid pseudorange

message.title: Weather truth from the plant
message.doc: The simulated weather the radar's sensor model renders: the storm cells and the stratiform area of weather_state_manager.py, which the plant moves with the wind and ages through their lifecycles as that module did, published once a second. The radar never sees this as weather; it renders a reflectivity volume from it, as reflectivity_simulator.py did, and processes that. Cells beyond cell_count and an absent area are zero. A cell's vertical profile is one of the two the Python used: entry_profile 0 is the profile of the initial cells (1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7 for the lowest four elevations, then 0.2), 1 the profile of cells that entered at the edge of the picture (1 - 0.15 per elevation, floor 0.2).

field.name: cell_1_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 1 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

field.name: cell_2_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 2 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

field.name: cell_3_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 3 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

field.name: cell_4_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 4 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

field.name: cell_5_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 5 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

field.name: cell_6_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 6 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

field.name: cell_7_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 7 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

field.name: cell_8_entry_profile
field.doc: Cell 8 vertical profile: 0 initial, 1 entered at the edge

message.title: Sensed flight state as received by the flight control computer
message.doc: Relayed by the bus controller from PLANT_SENSORS in the same minor frame (relays section). The FCS computes FCS_ATTITUDE, GCAS and the performance envelope from it.

message.title: Ground collision avoidance alerts
message.doc: groundCollisionAvoidanceSys.py, evaluated every frame: PULLUP when vertical speed is at or below -4000 ft/min and altitude is below 2000 ft; otherwise SINK_RATE when vertical speed is at or below -2000 ft/min; TERRAIN when the terrain clearance is below 500 ft; ALT_LOW when altitude is below 200 ft and TERRAIN is not set. PULLUP, SINK_RATE and TERRAIN are severity 1 (WARNING); ALT_LOW is severity 2 (CAUTION). The terrain clearance is the terrain-following radar's minimum clearance over the profile ahead (FCS_TERRAIN, from v1.4); while the radar provides none (not operating, no profile, or the message stale) there is no TERRAIN alert and the clearance SSM is NO_COMPUTED_DATA, as the Python's GCAS treated a missing TFR value. The values that drove the decision ride along so a display can show them without another message.

field.name: terrain_clearance
field.doc: The radar's minimum clearance ahead; negative when terrain ahead is above the aircraft

message.title: Flight envelope monitoring
message.doc: performaneMonitoring.py: an exceedance bit is set while the magnitude of the parameter is above its limit - g 9.0, angle of attack 25 deg, roll 60 deg, pitch 45 deg, vertical speed 6000 ft/min. Fuel efficiency is airspeed / (fuel flow / 60) in nm per kg and is NO_COMPUTED_DATA until the engine terminal publishes fuel flow.

message.title: Terrain clearance as received by the flight control computer
message.doc: The terrain-following radar's guidance, relayed. The ground collision avoidance function reads min_clearance when clearance_ssm is NORMAL and the message is fresh (stale after three periods, 0.3 s); otherwise it has no terrain clearance, as groundCollisionAvoidanceSys.py had none when the TFR gave it nothing.

block.title: Weather radar products
block.replaces: weather_radarVILResponse DISPLAY_VIL_DATA weather_radarData radarDataRequest radarDataResponse weather_radarPrecipitationResponse
block.doc: Everything one scan produced, published as one block when the scan completes so a consumer always draws a consistent picture (README section 8). Which sections are filled depends on the mode: SURVEILLANCE fills vil, precip and cells; MAPPING and PRECIPITATION fill precip and areas; WINDSHEAR fills windshear; TURBULENCE fills turbulence. Positions are polar from the aircraft: true azimuth and range. The record limits apply after the selection described in the README (the Python's own limits for the VIL and precipitation points; new for the rest); the counts before the limits are in RDR_WX_SCAN. The segment subaddress is polled every frame, so an 18-segment block arrives in 0.36 s, well inside the 1.2 s scan.

field.name: mode
field.doc: Mode of that scan; NONE with every section empty when the radar is not scanning

section.title: Vertically integrated liquid
section.doc: vil_data_generator_sync: VIL per column, the significant columns of the 8x-downsampled field, at most 20 chosen for continuity with the previous scan and then by cluster intensity

field.name: value
field.doc: VIL as the Python computed it: 3.44e-3 x Z^(4/7) x layer thickness, summed over the elevations

field.name: show_values
field.doc: 1 = intensity above 0.3: the display labels the point

section.title: Precipitation points
section.doc: precipitation_data_generator_sync: the Marshall-Palmer rate of each column's strongest return, the significant columns of the 8x-downsampled field, at most 15 chosen as the VIL points are

field.name: type
field.doc: By rate: HAIL above 50, MIXED above 25, RAIN above 10, else SNOW three times in ten, RAIN otherwise

section.title: Storm cells
section.doc: stormCellTracking.StormCellTracker: connected regions above 30 dBZ in the composite (maximum over elevation) field, tracked from scan to scan by proximity (5 bins); the 12 largest by size, then reflectivity, are reported

field.name: cell_id
field.doc: Tracker id, kept while the cell is followed

field.name: size
field.doc: Region size, half a nautical mile per bin as the Python counted it

field.name: azimuth_rate
field.doc: Centroid motion since the previous scan

field.name: range_rate
field.doc: Centroid motion since the previous scan

field.name: altitude
field.doc: The Python's cell-top estimate: size (as a range proxy) x tan(elevation)

field.name: vertical_development
field.doc: Change of that estimate per scan interval

section.title: Precipitation areas
section.doc: precipitation_analysis.PrecipitationAnalyzer: connected regions above 30 dBZ, with the Marshall-Palmer rate of their mean reflectivity and a type from it; the 12 strongest by reflectivity are reported

field.name: type
field.doc: HAIL above 55 dBZ, HEAVY_RAIN above 45, else RAIN

section.title: Wind shear events
section.doc: weather_processor.WindShearProcessor on the lowest elevation: shear proxy = 0.8 x |azimuthal reflectivity gradient| in kt/nm, an event where that is 15 or more and reflectivity 20 dBZ or more, one per 5x5-bin cluster, in order of severity; the first 20 are reported

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Beam height at the bin: range x tan(lowest elevation)

section.title: Turbulence cells
section.doc: weather_processor.TurbulenceProcessor on the lowest elevation: spectrum width proxy = local 3x3 standard deviation of reflectivity, EDR proxy = 0.3 x width^(2/3) / range_m^(1/3), a cell where EDR is 0.1 or more, reflectivity 15 dBZ or more and width at least 1, one per 4x4-bin cluster, strongest first; the first 20 are reported

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Beam height at the bin: range x tan(lowest elevation)

block.title: TFR elevation profile
block.doc: The terrain profile the radar assessed, sample by sample with its clearance level and terrain warning, and the path optimiser's altitude commands, as tfr_radar.py's elevation profile and terrain warning messages carried them to the display. Sample i is at ground distance i x range_m / (samples - 1) ahead along the heading; the samples are the profile section's records. The block is republished when a new profile has been assessed and at least 15 frames (0.3 s) have passed since the last one, so a 10-segment block always arrives whole; the guidance message carries the latest assessment every frame. An empty profile with mode NONE is published when the radar stops operating.

field.name: profile_seq
field.doc: terrain_seq of the PLANT_TERRAIN profile assessed

field.name: mode
field.doc: Mode the radar was in; NONE with every section empty when not operating

field.name: range_m
field.doc: Ground distance of the last sample

field.name: commands_truncated
field.doc: 1 = the path optimiser produced more commands than the section holds; the nearest are kept

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Aircraft altitude the profile was assessed against

field.name: set_clearance
field.doc: Set clearance the path was computed for

field.name: min_clearance
field.doc: The smallest clearance over the profile

section.title: Assessed terrain profile
section.doc: One record per terrain sample, nearest first: the elevation, the clearance level of that sample against the aircraft's altitude (ClearanceManager), and the terrain warning of that sample (HIGH_TERRAIN above 1500 m, else STEEP_TERRAIN when more than 300 m from 1000 m)

field.name: elevation
field.doc: Terrain height above mean sea level

section.title: Path altitude commands
section.doc: PathOptimiser.compute_path over the samples within the 9260 m look-ahead window: the required altitude is the highest terrain in a sliding window of max(5, n / 10) samples plus the set clearance, rate-limited to 25 m/s of altitude change at the aircraft's speed, a command emitted when it moves by more than 20 m from the last one, and a final CLEARANCE command at the window's end when the last command is below the window's highest terrain plus the set clearance. Nearest first

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Commanded altitude above mean sea level

block.title: Terrain profile ahead, from the plant
block.doc: What the terrain-following radar's antenna would measure: the terrain elevation at evenly spaced ground distances ahead of the aircraft along its heading, from the aircraft (sample 0) to range_m (the last sample), 100 samples over 10 km as tfr_radar.py's profile was. The plant samples its terrain, a fixed function of position (fmofp_plant.terrain), at the aircraft's position and heading every tenth of a second; sample i is at distance i x range_m / (samples - 1), the samples being this block's elevation records. The four segments take four frames, so a profile is complete at the radar before the next one is published.

field.name: range_m
field.doc: Ground distance of the last sample

section.title: Terrain elevation samples
section.doc: Nearest first; the record count is the sample count

field.name: elevation
field.doc: Terrain height above mean sea level

block.title: Terrain profile as received by the radar
block.doc: The relayed PLANT_TERRAIN: the bus controller writes the plant's descriptor and segments here in the frames it polls them, and the radar reassembles the profile.

block.title: Weather radar products as received by the radar display
block.doc: The relayed RDR_WX_PRODUCTS. The display draws a block once it has every segment of a version and the CRC matches, so it always shows one scan's consistent picture; a half-arrived scan is never drawn.

block.title: TFR elevation profile as received by the radar display
block.doc: The relayed RDR_TFR_ELEVATION: the terrain profile the terrain display draws, with its clearance levels and the path commands.

mode_code.name: TRANSMIT_STATUS_WORD
mode_code.doc: BC health poll; also how the BC reads the message-error bit after a no-response

mode_code.name: INITIATE_SELF_TEST
mode_code.doc: Starts initiated BIT; results in the BIT word

mode_code.name: INHIBIT_TERMINAL_FLAG
mode_code.doc: Terminal flag bit forced to 0 in the status word

mode_code.name: RESET_REMOTE_TERMINAL
mode_code.doc: Terminal re-initialises: state INITIALIZING, latched faults cleared

mode_code.name: TRANSMIT_VECTOR_WORD
mode_code.doc: After a service request: data word = SA (bits 4-0) the terminal wants serviced

mode_code.name: SYNCHRONIZE_WITH_DATA
mode_code.doc: Sent to broadcast RT 31 at the start of every minor frame. Data word: bits 15-6 major frame count (mod 1024), bits 5-0 minor frame 0-49

mode_code.name: TRANSMIT_LAST_COMMAND
mode_code.doc: Returns the last command word received

mode_code.name: TRANSMIT_BIT_WORD
mode_code.doc: Returns the BIT word (same layout as TERM_STATUS word 2)
